Aim: To implement a Student Management System using the Layered (N-tier) architecture, separating
the presentation, business logic and data access layers. 
Theory 
Layered architecture divides an application into horizontal layers. Every layer has one responsibility and
may only talk to the layer directly below it, so a change in one layer does not ripple through the whole
system. 
• Presentation layer (StudentUI): takes input and displays results; contains no business rules. 
• Business logic layer (StudentService): validates marks and roll numbers, computes grades. 
• Data access layer (StudentRepository): the only layer that runs SQL on the SQLite database. 
• Advantages: separation of concerns, easy testing, any layer can be replaced (e.g. SQLite by
MySQL) without touching the others.

Experiment 10: Producer–Consumer Message Queue 
Aim: To implement the Producer–Consumer problem using a bounded message queue with
asynchronous tasks. 
Theory 
In the Producer–Consumer pattern, producers create messages and put them in a shared queue, while
consumers take messages from it and process them. The queue decouples both sides, so they can work at
different speeds. 
• A bounded queue (maxsize = 3): put() waits when the queue is full and get() waits when it is
empty. 
• Two producer tasks and two consumer tasks run at the same time (Node.js is single-threaded, so
async tasks take the place of threads and no locks are needed). 
• A STOP sentinel is placed in the queue (one per consumer) for a clean shutdown.

Experiment 13: Circuit Breaker with Retry Mechanism 
Aim: To implement the Circuit Breaker pattern together with a retry mechanism using exponential
back-off to make calls to an unreliable service fault tolerant. 
Theory 
Remote calls can fail temporarily. A retry mechanism repeats the call after a growing delay (exponential
back-off). A circuit breaker stops calls to a service that keeps failing, so the system fails fast and the
service gets time to recover. 
• CLOSED: calls pass through; failures are counted. When failures reach the threshold the circuit
becomes OPEN. 
• OPEN: calls are rejected immediately. After the recovery timeout the circuit becomes
HALF-OPEN. 
• HALF-OPEN: one trial call is allowed. If it succeeds the circuit CLOSES, otherwise it opens
again. 
• Retry delays: 0.1 s, 0.2 s, 0.4 s ... (base delay × 2^attempt).
